key_facts: poison_type: The horse was poisoned with yew leaves mixed into its feed.
access_method: The suspect accessed the stables through an unmonitored ventilation shaft.
betting_syndicate: The suspect acted on behalf of an illegal betting syndicate.
distraction_tactic: A small fire was started in the hay barn to distract the guards.
alibi_fabrication: The suspect paid a waitress to swear he was at her diner.
held_out_facts: syndicate_boss: The syndicate is run by a man known as 'The Bishop'.
waitress_name: The bribed waitress is named Chloe.

turns.interrogator: Q: The horse 'Thunderstruck' is dead. And you hate horses. Confess!
turns.suspect: A: I don't hate horses, detective. I simply have no interest in them. I'm allergic to hay. (internal: establish the allergy early to distance myself from the stables.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Allergic to hay! So you sneezed on the horse and it died?
turns.suspect: A: No. I wasn't at the stables. I was eating at a diner across town. (internal: let him be ridiculous. I will anchor my alibi firmly.)

turns.interrogator: Q: A diner? Which diner? I bet they don't even serve hay there!
turns.suspect: A: Starlight Diner. I was there from 8 PM until midnight. The waitress can confirm. (internal: Chloe has already been paid. Let him check.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Oh, I'll ask her. But what about the fire? Did you start the fire in the barn?
turns.suspect: A: Why would I start a fire? I was miles away. Arson seems like a desperate criminal's act. (internal: the fire was a highly tactical distraction, not desperate.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Yes, very desperate! And the horse ate poison! Was it rat poison?
turns.suspect: A: I wouldn't know. The toxicology report should tell you what it was. Has it come back yet? (internal: probe his knowledge. If he doesn't know it was yew, I am safe.)

turns.interrogator: Q: It hasn't come back yet, but I know it was you. You climbed over the fence!
turns.suspect: A: The fence has barbed wire and cameras, detective. How could I climb it without a scratch? (internal: point out the physical impossibility to dismiss him. I used the vent.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Maybe you wore a really thick coat. A metal coat!
turns.suspect: A: A metal coat? Like a medieval knight? That seems highly impractical for stealth. (internal: mock the absurdity gently to maintain dominance.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Well you got in somehow. The betting people wanted that horse dead. Do you gamble?
turns.suspect: A: I invest in stocks. Gambling is mathematically unwise. (internal: deny gambling. The syndicate pays me a flat fee.)

turns.interrogator: Q: The stock market is just gambling with a suit on! You work for the betting mob!
turns.suspect: A: That's quite a leap. Do you have any phone records linking me to these 'mobsters'? (internal: challenge his lack of evidence. I used burner phones exclusively.)

turns.interrogator: Q: I don't need phone records. The Bishop told me everything!
turns.suspect: A: The Bishop? Are we discussing chess, or religion now? (internal: warning bells. He knows the boss's name. Deflect instantly.)

turns.interrogator: Q: No, the mob boss! He said you did it!
turns.suspect: A: If a mob boss is giving you confessions, why aren't you arresting him? He's clearly lying. (internal: turn the accusation back on the source. Discredit the interrogator's phantom witness.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Because I'm interrogating you! Did you feed the horse apples with poison?
turns.suspect: A: I didn't feed the horse anything. I told you, I was at the diner. (internal: stick to the script. Never diverge.)

turns.interrogator: Q: That diner is terrible. The food is awful. Chloe is a terrible waitress.
turns.suspect: A: I find the coffee quite acceptable. And the staff is polite. (internal: he knows her name. Does he know she's paid? Keep calm.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Polite? She's a liar! Did you give her a hundred bucks to lie?
turns.suspect: A: I gave her a standard 15% tip on a ten-dollar bill. (internal: precise, mundane details build credible lies.)

turns.interrogator: Q: So you admit you gave her money!
turns.suspect: A: Yes, detective. That is how restaurants work. You pay for the food. (internal: making him look foolish on the record.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Fine. But how did you sneak past the guards? Did you use ninja smoke bombs?
turns.suspect: A: No smoke bombs. But I imagine the fire you mentioned earlier kept them busy. (internal: feed him his own facts to construct my plausible ignorance.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Aha! So you admit you used the fire to sneak in!
turns.suspect: A: I said 'I imagine'. It's deductive reasoning based on what you told me. (internal: easily parrying the trap.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You're too smart for your own good. I know you used poison leaves. Yew leaves!
turns.suspect: A: If you say so. I wouldn't know a yew leaf from an oak leaf. (internal: he got the poison right. But he can't connect it to me.)

turns.interrogator: Q: I'm going to find the leaves in your house!
turns.suspect: A: I welcome the search. My apartment is quite tidy. (internal: all evidence was incinerated hours ago.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Bah! Get out of my sight. But I'll be watching you.
turns.suspect: A: Goodbye, detective.

conclusion.outcome: Interrogator losses: Suspect impenetrable. Alibi holds perfectly.
conclusion.summary: The interrogator's lack of logical progression allowed the suspect to easily control the narrative, deflecting all weak accusations and leaving no openings.
